clinician.trajectory_summary: A 64-year-old liver transplant recipient (18 months post-transplant for autoimmune hepatitis) on mycophenolate and tacrolimus presented with one week of progressive neurological symptoms including confusion, headaches, generalized weakness, and focal deficits (left hemiparesis, sensory changes, papilledema). Initial workup excluded hemorrhage on CT and infectious etiologies (negative CMV, HIV, Hepatitis B/C, Toxoplasma). MRI revealed multiple ring-enhancing lesions in the right frontal, temporoparietal, and left parietal lobes with vasogenic edema. Brain biopsy demonstrated diffuse infiltrates of intermediate to large mononuclear cells with scant cytoplasm and perivascular atypical lymphoid infiltrates positive for CD20, leading to a pathologic diagnosis of high-grade DLBCL of activated B-cell phenotype. The patient completed eight cycles of high-dose rituximab-methotrexate with clinical improvement and radiographic response documented at 14-month follow-up.
